content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has released updated recommendations on maternal and newborn care to ensure a positive postnatal experience. This publication builds upon the 2014 document titled WHO recommendations on postnatal care of the mother and newborn. The updated guidelines aim to improve the quality of essential, routine postnatal care for women and newborns, with the ultimate goal of enhancing maternal and newborn health and well-being. The postnatal period, defined as the time immediately following the birth of a baby and extending up to six weeks (42 days), is a critical phase for women, newborns, and their families. Despite its importance, maternal and neonatal mortality and morbidity rates remain unacceptably high during this period. Additionally, opportunities to enhance maternal well-being and support nurturing care for newborns are often underutilized. Postnatal care services are a vital component of the continuum of maternal, newborn, and child care. They are essential for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to reproductive, maternal, and child health, including reducing maternal mortality rates and preventing avoidable deaths of newborns. In alignment with the SDGs and the Global Strategy for Women’s, Children’s, and Adolescents’ Health, postnatal care efforts must go beyond mere survival and coverage to focus on the quality of care provided. The WHO defines a positive postnatal experience as one in which women, newborns, and their families receive consistent information, reassurance, and support from motivated health workers. This experience should occur within a well-resourced and flexible health system that recognizes the needs of women and babies while respecting their cultural contexts. A positive postnatal experience lays the foundation for improved shortand long-term health and well-being for both mothers and newborns. This guideline consolidates new and existing recommendations on routine postnatal care for women and newborns, applicable in both facility-based and community-based settings, regardless of resource availability. It provides a comprehensive set of recommendations for care during the postnatal period, focusing on the essential package of care that all women and newborns should receive. The emphasis is placed on the quality of care, encompassing both the provision and the experience of care. The updated guideline expands upon the 2014 WHO recommendations and complements existing WHO guidelines on managing postnatal complications. It is intended to inform the development of national and subnational health policies, clinical protocols, and programmatic guides. The target audience includes policymakers, healthcare providers, and program implementers responsible for maternal and newborn health services.
